A controller that charges an electric car from the surplus of a rooftop solar array, and the pytest suite that
proves it keeps three promises that pull against each other.

### The three promises, measured over a whole ordinary day

- **Buy nothing.** 277 Wh of the 36.4 kWh that reached the car came off the grid: **0.8 %**.
- **Sell nothing the car could take.** **4.9 %** of what the roof made went to the grid while the car had room.
- **Leave the car alone.** 47 changes to the offer in thirteen hours, and the session was stopped 8 times.

Seven days are measured, from a clear sky to a cloud every quarter of an hour. The numbers are in the README and
on the page; the budgets are in the test file.

### What is in it

- **125 tests**: 100 across three kinds of wallbox and 25 browser tests of the visual page. Every test is one
  plain sentence.
- **One control law, three wallboxes.** Straight into the model, over **Modbus TCP** the way a home wallbox is
  driven, and over **OCPP 1.6J** the way a public charge point is. A test replays a whole day through all three
  and compares them decision by decision.
- **37 of 37 planted bugs caught**, with a passing control run.
- **Five visual pages** (EN/RU): the project in two minutes, a live house you can send clouds over and sabotage,
  the whole-day chart with the grid line on zero, the last run replayed with the watt-hours each check measured,
  and the bug hunt.
- The page's JavaScript twin makes **88 560 identical decisions across 20 days**, eight of them generated at
  random.

### What it covers

The arithmetic and why it rounds down · the 6 A floor of IEC 61851-1 and the hysteresis around it · riding out a
cloud, and the budget that ends it · a kettle is a cloud as far as the meter is concerned · one phase or three,
and why the obvious threshold is the wrong one · a meter that has gone quiet · the Modbus register map and its
exceptions · an OCPP profile the station refuses · Hypothesis over days nobody wrote.

### Findings

Five, all fixed and pinned — including a fixed three-minute wait through shadows that bought 1.5 kWh on a day of
broken cloud, a phase threshold that moved the car onto wiring that could not carry it, and a planted bug that no
test could catch because two pieces of code were resetting the same clock.
[`docs/test-report.md`](https://github.com/NailKarimov/solar-surplus-charging/blob/main/docs/test-report.md),
section 3.

### Known limitation

No home battery. A hybrid inverter with storage changes the control law fundamentally — the battery masks the
surplus and competes with the car for it — and it was left out on purpose to keep one problem in view. That is
the next version.
